newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-49ERS BLANK EAGLES, STEELERS ROUT COLTS IN PLAYOFFS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-49ERS BLANK EAGLES, STEELERS ROUT COLTS IN PLAYOFFS.

text.p: The San Francisco 49ers blanked the Philadelphia Eagles 14-0 Sunday and the Pittsburgh Steelers shut out the Indianapolis Colts in the second half while rolling to a 42-14 rout in NFL playoff action Sunday.

The 49ers' Steve Young ran for a touchdown and overcame a rib injury to throw for the other in the NFC wild-card game at muddy 3COM Park, while the Steelers' Jerome Bettis ran for 102 yards and two one-yard scores in the AFC wild-card game at Three Rivers Stadium.

The 49ers, playing in the wild-card round for the first time since 1985, took advantage of an Eagles team that self-destructed in scoring position. San Francisco (13-4) won a trip to Green Bay to battle the Packers in next weekend's divisional playoffs.

Young was the 49ers' leading rusher with 67 yards on 12 carries. He scored on a nine-yard quarterback draw early in the second quarter, but suffered bruised ribs as he ricocheted off two Philadelphia defenders into the end zone.
Young left briefly but returned before the half ended as San Francisco took a 7-0 lead into intermission.
"I got hit in the ribs and couldn't breathe for a while until they gave me a shot," said Young. "I got better as it went on, but I couldn't throw in the rest of the first half."
"Steve Young doesn't give in to injury or circumstances," said San Francisco coach George Seifert. "He couldn't throw and he played in pain."

Early in the third quarter, Young hurled a 36-yard pass to Jerry Rice, who made a spectacular one-handed catch and raced to the Eagles 3-yard line. On the next play, Young and Rice hooked up again for a touchdown to make it 14-0.

Then the Niners' defence took over, knocking quarterback Ty Detmer out of the game and giving backup Mark Rypien no chance to engineer a comeback. Detmer was 14-for-21 for 148 yards with two interceptions.
"The wind and rain made it tough, but it was the same for both teams," said Young. "We got it done and our defence stopped them."

The Eagles had dominated the first half, holding the ball for more than 19 minutes, outgaining San Francisco 189-92 and getting in scoring position three times. But Gary Anderson hooked a 40-yard field goal attempt and Detmer was intercepted on the Eagles' next two trips inside the 20.
Former 49er Ricky Watters finished with 57 yards on 20 carries, but was limited to nine yards in the second half.
"I had to listen to them (his former teammates) the entire fourth period," the normally brash, outspoken running back said. "I can't believe we didn't score."

"This will take me a month to get over," said Philadelphia coach Ray Rhoades, a former San Francisco assistant. "We had Young banged up and got down in the red zone twice and messed it up. We didn't play well and they deserved to win, but I'm hurt, disappointed and really upset."
In Pittsburgh, the Steelers produced their best-ever post-season output -- 42 points, 29 of them in the second half -- in a rematch of last season's AFC championship game.
The Steelers (11-6), the AFC Central Division winners, will visit the Eastern champs, the New England Patriots, in next weekend's divisional playoffs.
The Colts have not defeated Pittsburgh, which is two wins away from returning to the Super Bowl, in 12 years.

Indianapolis (9-8) was outplayed in the first half, falling behind 13-0, but managed a 14-13 lead at the intermission after Steelers starting quarterback Mike Tomczak threw two interceptions, one resulting in a 59-yard touchdown return by Eugene Daniel and the other leading to a TD.

Bettis's first scoring plunge and Kordell Stewart's two-point conversion pass in the third quarter gave Pittsburgh the lead for good, 21-14, after a 16-play, 91-yard march that devoured the first 9:30 of the second half. Bettis carried seven times for 38 yards on the drive.

"At the end of the first half, we thought we had given them 14 points. We pretty much put them back in the game," Bettis said. "For the second half, we said we were going to go down and score on the first drive."
"I don't know if I've seen a drive that took up that much time that was executed that well," Steelers coach Bill Cowher said.
"In the first half we stopped ourselves. In the second, we came out with energy and emotion, got the crowd back in it and fed off that."

Bettis ran in from a yard out again to make it 28-14 39 seconds into the fourth quarter following a fumble by Marshall Faulk. Pittsburgh safety Carnell Lake apeared to be offsides before forcing and recovering the fumble.

"I thought Carnell Lake may have been offsides. If he was, he was, if he wasn't, he wasn't," Colts coach Lindy Infante said. "There were a lot of points scored today. I can't blame the whole ballgame on that play."
Stewart, Pittsburgh's alternate quarterback, ran for two touchdowns and 48 yards on nine carries as the Steelers pounded out 231 yards on the ground.
"It was just one of those days where I didn't have to throw it, I had to use my legs today," said Stewart.

Pittsburgh had the ball 15 minutes more than Indianapolis. Colts quarterback Jim Harbaugh was sacked four times -- three by linebacker Chad Brown. Harbaugh was 12-of-32 for 134 yards with one interception.
The Colts were limited to 146 total yards, just 22 in the second half. Indianapolis managed just 41 yards on the ground.
